Subject: Quick Q: badge scanners + QR fallback for CloudWest booth

Hi Vanessa —

We're finalizing our scanner hardware and wanted to confirm two things before we sign off: 1) BadgeCo's default scanner firmware will push raw badge IDs to a CSV; can your team accept a nightly bulk ingest or do you need real-time sync into HubSpot? 2) We want a QR fallback form if the scanner fails (battery, connectivity). Do you have an approved consent snippet we can present on that form?

Attaching BadgeCo's current spec for the device.

Thanks,
Jill Tanner

Hi Jill —

Thanks for the spec — looks fine. Quick answers up front: we prefer near real-time sync into HubSpot but can accept nightly bulk if BadgeCo's device only supports offline dumps; we'll need a small connector step to dedupe by email/badge id. For the QR fallback, yes — we need an explicit opt-in checkbox and a short consent string (1–2 lines) linking to our privacy page.

Operational asks for BadgeCo: please configure the scanner to emit a UUID badge_id and also capture the attendee email when available. If email isn't captured at scan-time the QR fallback should collect email + name + opt-in checkbox.

Can @tessa confirm the offline sync flow and @marissa draft the consent copy we can present on the fallback form? @ben, any HubSpot field concerns we should handle now (lifecycle stage, source, campaign mapping)?

I'll attach the spec to the thread for visibility.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Field Marketing Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Adding a couple HubSpot notes:

- We should map scans and form submissions into a single "CloudWest Expo 2026" contact property for dedupe (badge_id property + email fallback). Use badge_id as a unique external_id when present.
- If attendee already exists, do not create new leads; instead append an event-engagement activity and set lifecycle stage to "opportunity" only after a Sales qualification action. For now set source=event and event_campaign=cloudwest2026.
- HubSpot form embed is fine for real-time ingestion; will send a CSV mapping for the required fields. If BadgeCo only provides CSV dumps we'll run a nightly ingestion job and flag duplicates for manual review.

Please confirm whether legal requires any additional consent verbiage for marketing emails beyond the opt-in box.

— Ben Carter
AE, Redwood Inference

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, BadgeCo Ops <exhibitor-scan@badgeco.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick Q: badge scanners + QR fallback for CloudWest booth

Thanks — operational clarifications from our side:

- Devices will run in hybrid mode: real-time POST when on cellular/Wi-Fi, otherwise store locally and upload to BadgeCo cloud when connected. BadgeCo will provide nightly export CSV if needed.
- We will configure the scanner to attempt an email lookup via the badge QR payload. If email missing, the QR fallback form will be served (short form, mobile-friendly).
- Offline dedupe: the device will write badge_id + timestamp + scanned_email(optional) to the CSV. Ingest process will attempt matching by badge_id then email.
- Battery/backup: we will have 2 hot-swappable power packs per device; if scanner fails, booth staff will hand participants the QR printed card.

@Marissa — can you finalize consent language and include a link to our privacy page? I'm pasting the current short copy below as a starting point.

On Wed, Nov 18, 2026 at 11:03 AM vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com wrote:
> Operational asks for BadgeCo: please configure the scanner to emit a UUID badge_id and also capture the attendee email when available. If email isn't captured at scan-time the QR fallback should collect email + name + opt-in checkbox.

— Tessa Morgan
Field Ops Lead, Redwood Inference

Draft consent language (v3) — please review and flag any legal/ops conflicts: 

"By providing my contact information I agree to receive product updates and event follow-ups from Redwood Inference. I can unsubscribe at any time. See our Privacy Policy: https://redwood.com/privacy."

Notes:
- Kept it short for mobile form and clear opt-in.
- Legal suggested adding "event follow-ups" rather than a broad "marketing" phrase.
- Checkbox must be unchecked by default.

If we need a slightly longer version for EU attendees (GDPR), I can prepare that copy and include the lawful basis language.

Attachment: consent_language_v3.docx
